reason: The proposed right-hand ¹C₄ chair and per-3,6-anhydro-β-cyclodextrin structure are chemically consistent with the source and independent primary literature. However, the Lean development does not substantively derive either output: task-specific chemistry, chair selection, molecular connectivity, and stereochemistry are encoded directly in result-shaped definitions and then proved mainly by definitional reduction. The product graph is also not formally linked to the reaction state.

coverage.evidence: The right-hand template is the inverted ¹C₄ chair, matching the source image and independent literature. Nevertheless, warmAqueousBase36Closure directly assigns .oneCFour, favourableTemplate is defined to return .right exactly when that assigned value occurs, and chair_conformation is proved by ⟨rfl, rfl⟩. No chemical favorability or source-template relation is established.

The asserted C3–O–C6 bridge, remaining C2–OH, seven α-(1→4)-linked repeats, neutral closed-shell graph, C42H56O28 formula, and retained α-D-gluco face assignments are semantically correct. But per36AnhydroBetaCD, ProductAdjacent, ProductStereo, and kGraph directly contain those results. base_closure_is_per36_anhydro is rfl, the exactness lemmas unfold the same definitions, and no formal relation connects kGraph/ProductStereo to ProblemInput.betaCD or Derived.reactionProduct.

unsupported_assumptions: TrustedChemistry.perPrimaryTosylation hardcodes complete C6-selective tosylation using only an equivalent count and a coarse repeat pattern; TsCl, pyridine, accessibility, and selectivity are absent from the formal premises.
TrustedChemistry.warmAqueousBase36Closure hardcodes both C3–O–C6 formation and the ¹C₄ chair without representing the printed NaOH/H₂O/60 °C conditions or proving a chemistry rule.
The final molecular graph and stereochemical predicate are constructed independently of the modeled reaction product, so their identification with K is only asserted by naming and conjunction.
The right-hand template is made synonymous with the desired chair through favourableTemplate rather than through an independently transcribed template-to-chair relation.
